messages.text: I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me pull up your details and the triage notes before I ask anything.

Sorry it turned up like that. Let's find out what is actually wrong before anything else.

Two quick things so I can start on the right foot:

1. Which model is it (for example NerdQaxe++, Hammer DC06, Nexus S1)?
2. What exactly does it do when you plug it in: nothing at all, screen on but no hashing, an error on the screen, a noise or smell?

If there is anything on the screen or in the web UI, a photo or screenshot is the fastest way for me to read it.

Hi, Hal here. I'm ready when you are.

To get started, just tell me which model arrived faulty and what it does when you power it up (nothing at all, screen on but not hashing, an error message, a noise or smell). A photo of the screen helps if there is one.

I’m having an issue with my Hammer Miner BC04 purchased from Helium Deploy. I previously contacted support about this but haven’t heard back.
Order number: Shop····
Item: Hammer Miner BC04 (6TH/s)
Ship to: (address hidden), Canada

Issue:
The miner was stuck in a reboot loop and now shows a blank screen that won’t flash. The fan is still running, but it appears the ASIC chips are not responding. The unit is not hashing. Couple days ago, it showed it connected to a pool but had zero hash rate. Now it’s not hashing

Could you let me know what the next step should be?

Thanks, that is a clear description and it narrows things a lot. Fans running plus a blank screen plus 0 TH/s while connected to a pool usually means the controller is alive but the hash board is not starting. The screen itself is a separate little module, so a blank screen on its own is not the real story.

First check, just this one: is the miner still reachable on your network?

1. Open your router's client list (or a scanner app like Fing) and look for the miner's IP.
2. Put that IP in a browser.
3. If the web UI opens, tell me what it shows for firmware version, chip / ASIC count, and any error line on the status or log page.

If it does not appear on the network at all, say so and we go down the power route instead.

Understood. Fans spin but it is off the network and the screen stays blank, so next rung is power delivery, which is the most common cause of exactly this on these units.

Next check:

1. Unplug it, wait 60 seconds, plug back in (cold boot) and watch the screen for the first 30 seconds.
2. If you have a second adapter of the same rating, or can borrow one, run it on that instead. Many stock bricks sag once the chips try to pull current, which gives a reboot loop then a dead-looking unit.

Two things to send me while you do that:

- A short video of the power up, from plug in to about 30 seconds, so I can see the screen and hear the fans.
- A clear photo of the serial number sticker on the unit.
- Also tell me what the adapter says on its label (volts and amps).

That tells me whether this is the power supply or the board itself, and I pass my findings straight to the team either way.
I had a second lilygo screen from another miner  it will come on however it doesn’t hash

Good, that is a useful swap: with the spare LILYGO fitted it boots and displays, so the controller is alive and the original screen is a separate problem. What we are left with is the chips not coming up.

Next check, on the working screen:

1. What does it show for hashrate, chip or ASIC count, and temperature?
2. Is there any error or fault text on it (anything like VREG, TPS, "0 chips", "ASIC not detected")?
3. With this screen on, does it now appear on your network, so the web UI opens?

A photo of that screen while it is running is ideal. If the UI opens, tell me the firmware version too, since a full reflash is the last software fix before I call it a board fault.

That is the key data point: a known-good screen also goes blank on this unit, so it is not the screen.

One last thing to rule out before I call it, and it is the one JD always wants answered: the power supply.

1. What does the adapter label say (volts and amps)?
2. Do you have another adapter of the same or higher rating you can run it on, even from another miner?

If it stays blank, off the network and not hashing on a second known-good adapter, that is a board-level fault and I pass my findings to the team with everything we have tried. A short video of that attempt and a photo of the serial sticker will speed it up on their side.
Yes, set boots up and then I get this air and then it gets zero hash

So on the second adapter it does boot and then shows an error, then drops to zero hash. I need to read that error before I call this, and I will not guess at its meaning.

Can you send a photo of the screen with the error on it, or type the exact wording and any code it gives?

If it is anything in the VREG / TPS / "ASIC 0 chips" family, that is the voltage regulator on the board and no setting will fix it. If it is a pool or firmware message, we can fix it today.
